narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To explain the dominance of physical media sales over digital sales in Japan and the regulatory factors driving this trend.

units.meaning: Physical media sales are the largest share of the Japanese market at 77.1%.

basis.note: Physical ring segment value from table

accepted_routes: Physical accounts for 77.1% of Japanese sales.
Physical is the largest segment at roughly three-quarters of sales.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Physical ring segment must be visible and labeled or directly text-labeled with 77.1% or a rounded equivalent such as 77%.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state the Physical share as 77.1% or a rounded equivalent, rather than only implying it from ring size?

units.meaning: Digital sales are 12.5% of Japanese sales, much smaller than physical.

basis.note: Digital ring segment value from table

accepted_routes: Digital accounts for 12.5% of Japanese sales.
Digital is the smaller labeled segment at only 12.5%.
Digital represents roughly one-eighth of sales.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Digital ring segment must be visible and labeled or directly text-labeled with 12.5% or a rounded equivalent such as 13%.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video use the table's 12.5% Digital value rather than the narration's conflicting 18%?

units.meaning: Physical share is much larger than Digital share: 64.6 percentage points higher and about 6.2 times Digital.
accepted_routes: Physical exceeds Digital by 64.6 percentage points.
Physical is more than six times Digital.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both Physical and Digital segments or values must be visible in the same chart so the gap or ratio can be compared.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'nearly the opposite' / physical-and-digital contrast clause
units.reviewer_question: Should the required comparison be expressed as a percentage-point gap, a ratio, or either?

units.meaning: Physical sales are more than half of the Japanese market, reinforcing its dominance.
accepted_routes: Physical is more than half of sales.
Physical is a majority of Japanese sales.
Physical's 77.1% share makes it the dominant majority.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Physical segment must appear larger than half of the ring, or the text must state that its 77.1% share is more than half.
units.reviewer_question: Is an explicit 'more than half' or majority statement required, or is the 77.1% share and comparison enough?

units.meaning: The unlabelled segment is 10.4% of the ring and is smaller than Digital, completing the chart total.
accepted_routes: The unlabelled segment is 10.4% of the ring.
Physical and Digital together are 89.6%, leaving 10.4% unlabelled.
The unlabelled segment is smaller than Digital (10.4% vs 12.5%).
units.visual_evidence_rule: The unlabelled ring segment must be visible and distinguishable, or the chart must otherwise account for the remaining 10.4%.
units.temporal_anchor: after the physical and digital share clauses, before any regulatory context
units.reviewer_question: Should the video include the unlabelled 10.4% segment, or omit it as optional chart noise?

optional_valid: Combined Physical + Digital = 89.6%, leaving the unlabelled segment at 10.4%.
A qualitative mention of copyright or licensing restrictions as context, provided it is not quantified or asserted as the exact cause of the 77.1/12.5 split.
Rounding shares to 77% and 13% for readability.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that copyright laws caused the exact 77.1% physical / 12.5% digital split; the table has no regulatory measure.
Using narration's 75% or 18% as data values when table values are 77.1% and 12.5%.
Treating the unlabelled 10.4% segment as Digital or Physical.
Extrapolating to future trends or countries outside Japan.
Saying Digital is 12.5% of Physical; the table-based ratio is Physical / Digital = 77.1 / 12.5 = 6.168.
notes: Table values conflict with the narration's 75% physical / 18% digital; use 77.1% and 12.5% as ground truth. Regulatory factors are context only and are not quantified by the table.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
